chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, who linked it up to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him),
He said: Three of the traditions of the Messengers are: perfume, trimming the hair, and frequent sexual intercourse.

key_terms.سُنَنِ: traditions or practices of the Prophets

ai.seo_question: What are the three traditions of the Messengers mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq presents these three practices as markers of affluence and beauty, linking personal grooming to spiritual and social dignity. While 'trimming hair' (iḥfāʾ) is often interpreted as shortening or keeping it neat rather than shaving, the emphasis on 'frequent sexual relations' (kathrat al-ṭarūqah) highlights the Prophetic ideal of maintaining marital intimacy as a means of spiritual contentment and defeating the devil. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on balancing asceticism with appreciation for worldly beauty and physical well-being as acts of worship.
